title: SSE streaming: robust chunk framing and reconnect semantics for streaming API
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a production-grade Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming protocol for the Core API that handles chunk framing, chunk flushing for low-latency tokens, and robust reconnect/resume behavior. This ticket covers the server-side framing format, client resume semantics (Last-Event-ID), compatibility fallbacks for older SDKs that expect chunked JSON, and operational settings to avoid proxy buffering. The goal is predictable, low-latency, and resumable streaming for text generation, function/tool call messages, and structured outputs.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits SSE-compliant event stream with Content-Type: text/event-stream and Transfer-Encoding: chunked
Each logical message has a stable monotonically increasing message_id that can be used with Last-Event-ID to resume
Keepalive comments (": <comment>\n\n") are emitted every 12s to prevent proxy buffering
Clients can resume a stream from a Last-Event-ID and receive any missing tokens or a restart flag if resume is impossible
Fallback path: endpoint supports chunked JSON (ndjson style) when client requests compatibility mode via Accept header
Automated integration tests simulate network drop and assert resume semantics and correctness of reconstructed output
Docs and SDK samples updated with reconnection examples and best-practices
implementation_notes: Payload format: JSON payloads with top-level keys: {"type": "token|function_call|done", "seq": <int>, "content": <string or object>} serialized as a single-line JSON in 'data:' to simplify client parsers

Chunk aggregation: for very small tokens, batch up to 64 tokens or 16KB before flush to avoid excessive calls; for latency-sensitive routes (low-latency profile), flush single-token frames immediately
Keepalive: send SSE comment lines (prefix ':') every 12s; also emit a lightweight 'event: ping' every 60s with empty payload for diagnostics

Resume semantics: server stores recent stream segments (ring buffer) keyed by request_id and message_id for the session TTL (default 30s) to support immediate resume; if missing, server returns 'event: restart_required' in initial response
Last-Event-ID: respect standard header; we also accept ?last_event_id= on websocket/SDK fallbacks for clients behind proxies that strip headers
Compatibility mode: Accept: application/x-ndjson+json triggers ndjson chunked responses (one JSON object per line) for legacy SDKs; this disables SSE 'event' lines
Tool/function calls: encode as 'event: function_call' with data.payload.function_name + args in data JSON; client SDKs will convert event into a function-call object and allow automatic invocation
Structured outputs: to support structured JSON outputs reliably, include a 'complete' message type with SHA256 digest of the concatenated structured output so clients can detect truncation
Proxy and CDN guidance: set 'Cache-Control: no-transform, no-store' and 'X-Accel-Buffering: no' where supported to avoid buffering by intermediaries
HTTP/2: SSE over HTTP/2 is not natively supported; for HTTP/2 we will use chunked NDJSON fallback and set 'x-redwood-stream-protocol: ndjson-v1' for telemetry
Authentication: require Authorization header; do not echo tokens in stream payloads; redact any sensitive tool output before streaming
Testing: end-to-end tests using tc/netem to introduce drop/delay, unit tests for last-event-id resume, load tests to verify memory overhead of ring buffer
qa_plan: Unit tests for SSE line framing and JSON payload serialization
Integration test: client reconnects at random offsets (drop after N messages) and asserts final reconstructed output equals baseline
Compatibility test: request with Accept: application/x-ndjson+json and validate ndjson lines parseable by legacy SDKs
Chaos test: simulate slow proxies that buffer for 30s to validate keepalive prevents buffering
Performance test: measure tokens/sec and p50/p95 latency for low-latency profile vs default profile
Security test: live pen-test to ensure no sensitive PII leaks in stream or logs
comments: 2026-03-01 Asha Patel: Initial ticket creation. Problem statement: unpredictable client experience when interrupted network causes partial token loss. Proposal: SSE with resume support and ndjson compatibility.

2026-03-03 Miguel Santos: Spike implemented prototype: server emits 'id' with monotonic seq and 'data' lines; basic resume by Last-Event-ID works when ring buffer size >= tokens-sent. Pushed branch: github.com/redwood-inference/core/compare/feat/sse-resume

2026-03-05 Design review (Lina Cho): suggested adding explicit 'event: function_call' and 'event: structured' to help SDK routing. Also requested clear examples in Console docs for interpreting partial structured outputs.

2026-03-07 Engineering note: decided to default to batching small tokens up to 16KB unless client sets 'x-stream-mode: low-latency' to avoid high small-packet costs for high throughput customers. Trade-off: slightly higher latency for small-token workloads vs reduced RPC overhead.

2026-03-09 Security review (Jon Reed): confirmed Authorization header is sufficient; flagged that proxies may cache streams if Cache-Control missing. Added header guidance and X-Accel-Buffering setting.

2026-03-12 Miguel Santos: Integration tests added. Simulated network drop at 50% progress; resume succeeded in 92/100 runs. Failures traced to ring buffer TTL (30s) being too short under extreme GC pauses. Increasing TTL to 60s for retries while monitoring memory impact.

2026-03-14 Asha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to require documentation and SDK examples. Opening PR for API docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/SSE+Streaming+Spec and implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/core/pull/1987
